title: CosciaLab/histo pipeline parameters
description: Processing, segmentation and quantification of multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) images

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to a comma-separated samplesheet. Its shape depends on use_preprocessing: one row per acquisition cycle when true, one row per sample when false.
input.help_text:
Two shapes are accepted and the correct one is validated at runtime, so no fixed schema is declared here.

use_preprocessing = true (default): one row per cycle, with columns sample, cycle_number, image_tiles and marker_sheet, and optionally dfp and ffp. Validated against assets/schema_input_cycle.json.

use_preprocessing = false: one row per stitched image, with column data_path and optionally sample (default: the file name). Validated against assets/schema_input.json. Use this for pre-stitched images and for dearrayed TMA cores re-entering the pipeline.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. Use an absolute path.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

preprocessing.title: Preprocessing
preprocessing.description: Illumination correction, stitching and registration, optional background subtraction and optional TMA dearray. These run before the image enters the SpatialData half, and are skipped entirely when use_preprocessing is false.

use_preprocessing.description: Run the preprocessing half: illumination correction, stitching and registration, and the optional steps below. When false, each samplesheet row is an already stitched OME-TIFF, such as a dearrayed core re-entering the pipeline.
use_preprocessing.help_text: **Requires:** `instanseg_channels` when `use_instanseg` is true and this is false. **Conflicts:** `preprocessing_only`, `use_projection` and `use_tma_dearray` when this is false.

preprocessing_only.description: Stop after preprocessing: keep the stitched images under preprocessing/ and skip segmentation, quantification and the QC report. Ashlar's own QC is still written when use_qc is true. Requires use_preprocessing; no segmentation method is needed.

skip_reference_dna_check.description: Run even when Ashlar's alignment channel or Coreograph's dearray channel is not a dna channel in the marker sheet. A warning is logged instead of stopping.

ashlar_args.description: Extra command-line arguments passed through to Ashlar.
ashlar_args.help_text:
Ashlar runs from the josenimo/ashlar image, which adds rotation correction between cycles; `-c -1` aligns each cycle on its own last channel. Do not pass `--qc-output` or `--report`: the pipeline adds them when use_qc is true.

**Requires:** `-c` (a within-cycle channel index, default 0, -1 for the last) to be a `dna` channel in every cycle of the marker sheet, unless `skip_reference_dna_check` is true.

use_backsub.description: Subtract background channels after stitching. Requires exposure and background columns in the marker sheet.
use_backsub.help_text: **Conflicts:** `cellpose_channels` or `instanseg_channels` naming a channel marked `remove` in the marker sheet.

backsub_args.description: Extra command-line arguments passed through to backsub.

use_tma_dearray.description: Split a tissue microarray into individual cores with UNetCoreograph. Each core then runs the downstream half as an independent sample, and the results are merged per slide at the end. Requires use_preprocessing.

tma_expected_cores.description: Total number of cores expected on the slide. Required with use_tma_dearray unless coreograph_args is set.
tma_expected_cores.help_text:
Count the cores you expect to find, not rows times columns: arrays have empty or lost positions. The pipeline tries several Coreograph downsample factors and keeps the one whose cores best match this count and tma_core_diameter_mm. Every slide in the run is scored against the same values, so run arrays of different layouts separately.

**Requires:** `tma_core_diameter_mm`. **Ignored unless:** `use_tma_dearray` is true and `coreograph_args` is unset.

tma_core_diameter_mm.description: Expected core diameter in mm. Required with use_tma_dearray unless coreograph_args is set.
tma_core_diameter_mm.help_text:
Used with tma_expected_cores to choose Coreograph's downsample factor. The pixel size is read from the image's OME-XML.

**Requires:** `tma_expected_cores`. **Ignored unless:** `use_tma_dearray` is true and `coreograph_args` is unset.

coreograph_args.description: Command-line arguments for UNetCoreograph. Setting this skips the downsample sweep.
coreograph_args.help_text:
Leave unset to let the pipeline choose --downsampleFactor from tma_expected_cores and tma_core_diameter_mm (it then runs on the marker sheet's first dna channel with --buffer 2 --sensitivity 0.3). Set it, for example to '--downsampleFactor 4 --channel 0 --buffer 2', to run Coreograph exactly as given.

**Requires:** a `--channel` index (default 0) that is a `dna` channel in the marker sheet, unless `skip_reference_dna_check` is true. **Ignored unless:** `use_tma_dearray` is true.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).

patches.title: Patches
patches.description: Tiling of the image before segmentation

patch_width_pixel.description: Width and height of each segmentation patch, in pixels. Choose it so the image yields roughly 16 to 200 patches: patch_width = sqrt(width * height / target_patches).
patch_width_pixel.help_text:
This parameter sets how segmentation parallelises, and it is not automatic. Tiled segmentation is the reason this pipeline scales, but only if the tiling suits the image.

Too large and you get one patch and no parallelism at all: a 3138 x 2511 image at patch_width_pixel = 5000 produces a single task. Too small and you get thousands of tasks, each paying container startup and scheduler overhead; a 115000 x 115000 image at 2000 produces 3364 of them.

Task count is usually the constraint, so aim for a few times your cluster's concurrency and no more. Memory can be too: InstanSeg on a 5000 pixel patch of 6 channels needed more than 12 GB.

Rough guide, patches = ceil(width/p) * ceil(height/p):
  3k x 3k      -> 1000 gives 9,    2000 gives 4,    5000 gives 1
  25k x 25k    -> 2000 gives 169,  5000 gives 25,   8000 gives 16
  50k x 50k    -> 5000 gives 100,  8000 gives 49,   10000 gives 25
  115k x 115k  -> 8000 gives 225,  10000 gives 144, 15000 gives 64

Get the dimensions of a stitched image with: python -c "import tifffile; print(tifffile.TiffFile('stitched.ome.tif').series[0].shape)"

patch_overlap_pixel.description: Overlap between neighbouring patches, in pixels. About twice a cell diameter.

use_gpu.description: One GPU per Cellpose and InstanSeg patch task. Cluster only; InstanSeg then takes at most 10 channels.

tissue_segmentation.title: Tissue segmentation
tissue_segmentation.description: Parameters related to the tissue segmentation

level.description: Level of the image pyramid to use for tissue segmentation

mode.description: Mode for the tissue segmentation: 'staining' or 'saturation' (for H&E images).

tissue_segmentation_kwargs.description: Additional tissue segmentation parameters as a python dict string

filtering.title: Cell filtering
filtering.description: Filtering objects at segmentation. Cells are never dropped at aggregation.

min_area_pixels2.description: Objects smaller than this, in pixels², are dropped at segmentation, per patch. Unset: sopa uses 0.

expand_radius_ratio.description: Expand cell polygons by `expand_radius_ratio * mean_radius` when measuring channel intensities, for X only; the nucleus and cytoplasm layers, area and centroids use the unexpanded shapes. Helps capture membrane stainings at the cell boundary.

quantification_statistics.description: Per-marker statistics, comma-separated, no spaces: mean, median, std, min, max, q25, q75, q90. mean is required.
quantification_statistics.help_text: **Requires:** `mean` in the list, each statistic once.

image_preprocessing.title: Image preprocessing
image_preprocessing.description: Image preprocessing applied before segmentation (Cellpose, InstanSeg). Unset: sopa's per-method defaults (they differ for InstanSeg).

gaussian_sigma.description: Parameter for scipy gaussian_filter (applied before running the segmentation method)

clip_limit.description: Parameter for skimage.exposure.equalize_adapthist (applied before running the segmentation method)

clahe_kernel_size.description: Parameter for skimage.exposure.equalize_adapthist (applied before running the segmentation method)

projection.title: Channel projection
projection.description: Segment a nuclear and a cell channel projected from many markers, for 2-channel Cellpose

use_projection.description: Project the marker sheet's channels into a nuclear and a cell (membrane and cytoplasm) channel and segment those with Cellpose. Requires use_cellpose and use_preprocessing; leave cellpose_channels unset.
use_projection.help_text: **Requires:** `use_cellpose` and `use_preprocessing`. **Conflicts:** `cellpose_channels`, and `keep_projection` when this is false.

keep_projection.description: Keep the projected nuclear and cell image in the published store as `<image>_projected`. Requires use_projection.

projection_method.description: How the rescaled markers of a channel are combined. max keeps markers that stain only one cell type at full brightness; mean averages out noise but dims them.

projection_low_percentile.description: Per-marker percentile mapped to 0 before combining. Zero-valued padding is ignored.

projection_high_percentile.description: Per-marker percentile mapped to 1 before combining.

projection_sigma.description: Gaussian smoothing in pixels applied to each marker before combining; 0 for none.

segmentation_targets.title: Segmentation targets
segmentation_targets.description: What each enabled method segments: whole cells, nuclei, or both.

segment_cells.description: Segment whole cells with each enabled method: shapes `{method}_cells`. Set false for nuclei only.

segment_nuclei.description: Segment nuclei with each enabled method: shapes `{method}_nuclei`. With segment_cells, nuclei are linked to cells and the cytoplasm is derived.

cellpose.title: Cellpose
cellpose.description: Parameters related to the cellpose segmentation method

use_cellpose.description: Segment with Cellpose. May be combined with use_instanseg.
use_cellpose.help_text: **Requires:** `cellpose_channels` unless `use_projection` is true, and `use_cellpose` or `use_instanseg` unless `preprocessing_only` is true.

cellpose_channels.description: Channel(s) to segment with Cellpose. Use marker names from the marker sheet, e.g. "DNA_1". If multiple, separate by space, comma or pipe characters. The last is the nuclear channel, which segment_nuclei uses.
cellpose_channels.help_text: **Conflicts:** `use_projection`, and channels marked `remove` in the marker sheet with `use_backsub`.

cellpose_kwargs.description: Additional cellpose parameters as a python dict string

instanseg.title: InstanSeg
instanseg.description: Parameters related to the InstanSeg segmentation method

use_instanseg.description: Segment with InstanSeg. May be combined with use_cellpose.
use_instanseg.help_text: **Requires:** `instanseg_pixel_size`, `instanseg_channels` when `use_preprocessing` is false, and `use_cellpose` or `use_instanseg` unless `preprocessing_only` is true. **Conflicts:** `use_gpu` on more than 10 channels.

instanseg_model_type.description: Name of the pretrained InstanSeg model, or path to a local model. sopa defaults to `fluorescence_nuclei_and_cells`

instanseg_pixel_size.description: Image resolution in microns per pixel. Required: without it InstanSeg does not rescale and may find no cells

instanseg_channels.description: Channel(s) to segment with InstanSeg. Unset takes them from each sample's marker sheet: `dna` and `marker` channels for `cells`, `dna` only for `nuclei`; autofluorescence, blank and removed channels are left out. Required without a marker sheet (`use_preprocessing = false`). Use marker names, separated by space, comma or pipe characters.
instanseg_channels.help_text: **Conflicts:** more than 10 channels with `use_gpu`, and channels marked `remove` in the marker sheet with `use_backsub`.

instanseg_kwargs.description: Additional InstanSeg parameters as a python dict string

qc_report.title: QC report
qc_report.description: Parameters related to the quality-control metrics and report

use_qc.description: Whether to compute QC metrics, write Ashlar's stitching and registration QC, and render the QC report
use_qc.help_text: Writes a machine-readable JSON of metrics next to a self-contained HTML report, per sample and method, into `<outdir>/qc`, plus `{sample}_comparison.json` and `.html` when both methods segment cells. The JSON is the contract an unattended run should read; the HTML is for a person. With use_preprocessing, Ashlar also writes its stitching and registration QC to `<outdir>/preprocessing/registration/{sample}_ashlar_qc/`, which the report reads.

use_qc_images.description: Whether to include the segmentation crops and the cell clustering in the QC report
use_qc_images.help_text: These cost minutes where the metrics cost seconds: the crops rasterise segmentation polygons and the clustering builds a nearest-neighbour graph over every cell. Set false for a metrics-only report. Tuning for this step goes through `ext.args` for QC_IMAGES in conf/modules.config.
